injury_names: Ankle roll (inversion/eversion) | Hip instability | Ankle sprain (ATFL tear)
injury_descriptions: The foot is rolled sideways at the ankle (inversion/eversion), the classic lateral ankle-sprain mechanism. A severe roll can injure the ATFL and other lateral ankle ligaments. | The pelvis is displaced far from the base of support, transferring excessive stress to the knee and ankle. | The foot is not aligned with the body's momentum, creating lateral shearing forces on the ankle ligaments.
injury_preventions: Land with the foot flat and pointed along the direction of movement; strengthen the peroneal muscles and practice stable single-leg landings. | Keep the hips centered over the feet and strengthen hip stabilizers for better control. | Land with the foot pointing along the direction of movement and keep the knee centered over the foot.
